subject: Quantapulse SLO & ops benchmark recap — reserved throughput validation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@quantapulse.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quantapulse SLO & ops benchmark recap — reserved throughput validation

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for taking the time today — useful call. Below is a concise recap of what we heard from your side, our preliminary sizing recommendations, and a proposed validation plan so we can lock an SLA-ready Dedicated pool that meets your latency and streaming requirements.

1) Business/traffic profile (what you told us)
- Production concurrency target: 120 concurrent live sessions during peak window (09:00–11:00 PT).
- Average tokens per session: 700 tokens (prompt + generated), with streaming enabled for the final 400 tokens on average.
- End-to-end latency SLO: 95th percentile generation latency <= 450 ms per token for streaming-enabled sessions; peak tail for cold-starts (first token) <= 900 ms.
- Day-1 steady-state throughput goal: 15M tokens/day, with growth to 45M within 6 months.

2) Preliminary capacity recommendations (engineering read)
- Preferred GPU candidates for validation: NVIDIA H100 80GB, NVIDIA A100 40GB (v5), and NVIDIA L4 for cost-sensitive inference of smaller models.
- Recommended reserved concurrency per GPU: H100 ~ 40 concurrent streaming sessions (large-context), A100 ~ 22–28, L4 ~ 8–12 (depends on model quantization).
- Suggested initial reserved pool: 3 x H100 (reserve) + 2 x A100 as overflow/burst (region us-west). This gives headroom for your 120 concurrent target while keeping burst fallback.

3) Acceptance criteria for Dedicated validation
- Functional: model parity vs hosted baseline (logprobs/sample checks).
- Latency: 95th token latency <= 450 ms for streaming sessions at target concurrency.
- Throughput: sustained token throughput >= 12M tokens/day per reserved pool (measured over 24h soak).
- Reliability: no more than 1% 5xx errors during soak.

4) Quick ops/implementation notes
- Prefix cache: enable per-customer prefix/KV cache to shave ~40–60 ms on repeated prompts in your use-case.
- Batching policy: conservative batching during peak (batch size 8–12) to avoid latency spikes; larger batches overnight for cost savings.
- Quantization path: evaluate Q4 and int8 paths on A100/L4 for smaller models.

5) Next steps & timeline
- Redwood: spin up a 48-hour smoke with 1 H100 + 1 A100 loaded with your canonical prompt set (we’ll provision by EOD Wed).
- QuantaPulse: share the canonical prompt set, three high-priority streaming flows, and sample production traces (anonymized) by Tue 02/09.
- Joint validation: schedule 90-minute check-in after the smoke to review perf logs and decide on the full reserved pool.

Attachments included: qpulse-slo-matrix.xlsx (SLO matrix and acceptance gates), qpulse-gpu-benchmark-log.txt (sample logs).

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the smoke and loop in infra to provision the reserved pool.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Samir Patel <samir@quantapulse.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Quantapulse Technical Ops <ops@quantapulse.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Feb 2027 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quantapulse SLO & ops benchmark recap — reserved throughput validation

Ben —

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers inline and a couple of clarifications:

- Concurrency: 120 concurrent sessions is correct for peak; we have vertical scaling in the client so concurrency can spike to ~150 for short bursts (sub-5 minute windows).
- Token profile: the 700 token average is correct. For streaming we almost always start streaming after the first 80–120 tokens.
- Latency SLO: 450 ms p95 is our target for user-facing streams; we can accept a slightly higher first-token warm-up (up to 1s) if subsequent tokens are <450 ms.

Questions for you:
1) For the suggested 3x H100 + 2x A100 config, what reserve throughput (tokens/sec) should we expect to bill for? We want a predictable monthly commit number to talk to finance.
2) If we prefer to prioritize cost, can we validate an all-A100 pool with more nodes and still hit the latency SLO when streaming?

We’ll pull together the prompt set and sanitized traces — expect that by EOD today. Also attaching our internal performance expectations doc for reference.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform, QuantaPulse
samir@quantapulse.ai
[attachment: qpulse-internal-perf-specs.pdf (pdf)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@quantapulse.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quantapulse SLO & ops benchmark recap — reserved throughput validation

Samir —

Short technical follow-up and confirmation of what we’ll measure during the smoke:

Planned smoke configuration (48h)
- GPUs: 1 x H100 (prod role) + 1 x A100 (burst role) in us-west-2.
- Model: qpulse-prod-embedder-v2 (sharded) + qpulse-chat-gen (causal LM, quantization on A100 path).
- Traffic profile: synthetic load replay of your traces mixed 70/30 (70% typical, 30% tail burst) with ramp to 120 concurrent over 10 minutes.

Metrics & gating (we will publish dashboards)
- p50/p95/p99 token generation latency (streaming enabled).
- First-token latency distribution for cold vs warm requests.
- Token throughput (tokens/sec), sustained 1h averages and 24h soak numbers.
- Error rates (4xx/5xx) and instance-level OOM / throttling events.
- Resource counters: GPU utilization, host networking (p95), and KV cache hit rate.

Benchmark-specific notes
- H100 path: expect to meet 95th token latency target at 120 concurrent for the configured models; we’ll confirm with the smoke.
- A100-only option: feasible but will likely need 60–80% more nodes (dependent on model quantization). We’ll capture model-specific perf curves in the run and provide a cost/latency tradeoff table.
- L4 suitability: only recommended for smaller, lower-quality models or heavy quantization; not our first choice for your streaming latency target.

Deliverables after smoke (48–72h)
- Per-GPU perf curves (throughput vs concurrency), annotated with cost estimate by reserved/ondemand billing.
- A recommended reserved pool sizing (min/max), fallback policy, and an ops playbook for failover to burst capacity.
- A DRT (decision readiness test) checklist you can present to finance/ops.

Please confirm if we should proceed with the smoke using your traces as soon as you drop them here. If you want a separate all-A100 smoke instead of the H100/A100 mix, say so and we’ll provision accordingly (lead time for additional A100 nodes ~ 48 hours).

- Priyom
Priyom Das
